messages:
ash: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression in canary this morning. Small/short sequences (<=64 tokens) latency spiked ~2.8x p50 after the kernel-selector tweak. Suspect our continuous-batcher is forming big mixed batches and long sequences are stealing slots.

maria: ugh. saw that in the dashboard too. p95 for short-tenant cohort jumped. Any traces/profiles yet? :eyes:

ash: grabbed a flamegraph from the canary host. Top is the new kernel cross-check path + spin in queue. Also KV cache hit-rate for short requests dropped from 0.67 -> 0.51. attaching quick snippet (from perf-ci):

perf-ci-bot: ```text
profile: host=canary-3
callers: kernel_selector::choose_fastpath 54%
         batcher::coalesce 18%
         kv_cache::evict_loop 12%
         request_dispatch::wait_spin 8%
``` 

maria: so two things: kernel choice bias + KV churn. Long sequences warm the KV and hold large prefixes in cache; our token_budget_target heuristic currently biases to fill by token-count which favors long seqs.

sam: idea — reserve a small fraction of microbatch slots for short-path handshake. e.g., `short_slot_reserve = 0.12` so short requests get quick admission without waiting behind long token-heavy admissions.

dina: +1. We should also consider queue policy: instead of global FIFO, maintain two admission queues (short/long) with dynamic weights. If short p50 goes above threshold, increase short weight. lightweight, no heavy refactor.

maria: also KV: when a long sequence uses huge KV, eviction pressure evicts small prefixes used by shorts. Could we change eviction policy to favor retaining recent small prefixes for tenants with high short-rate? maybe LRU with tenant-priority bump.

ash: rough config patch I tested locally:

perf-ci-bot: ```yaml
batching:
  token_budget_target: 512
  max_microbatch_tokens: 4096
  short_slot_reserve: 0.12    # fraction of microbatch concurrency
queue_policy:
  mode: dual-queue
  short_weight: 0.5
  long_weight: 0.5
kv_cache:
  eviction_policy: tenant_lru_bump
``` 

sam: that looks reasonable. metrics to track for the experiment: per-tenant short p50/p95, overall throughput, KV hit-rate by length bucket, kernel_selector fastpath rate.

dina: need to be careful about tail regressions for long sequences. If we over-favor shorts, long throughput might collapse. propose an automatic hedging: short_weight = min(0.7, base + A*(short_p50_ratio-1)).

maria: agreed. also add a guard: if overall GPU utilization falls below 60% for >30s, scale short_weight down — keep unit-economics sensible.

ash: I'll sketch an experiment plan — A/B on 10% of traffic in canary region. 3 hosts with the dual-queue + short_slot_reserve. Run for 2 hours, then 24h run if stable. collect: per-tenant latency histogram, kernel selection counts, kv hit/miss by tenant, microbatch composition stats.

sam: can you also log microbatch composition? i.e., list of seq-lengths per microbatch (sampled). that will prove the slot-reserve effect.

ash: yes. added sample logging (1/1000) to avoid blowup.

perf-ci-bot: deploy triggered: canary/slot-reserve-experiment -> canary-3, canary-4, canary-5

ops-bot: Deploy started by ash at 2026-03-18T14:02:10Z. Rolling updates across canary pool.

maria: one more thought — kernel-selector fallback path currently does a synchronous recompile check when it sees a new shape, which stalls. maybe change to async probe + optimistic continue on slower kernel to avoid blocking short requests.

dina: yep lazy probe + telemetry flag sounds good. add `kernel_probe_mode: async_probe` to the canary config.

ash: action items:
  - ash: roll experiment + enable dual-queue + short_slot_reserve (in progress)
  - sam: implement microbatch sampling + dashboard panel (ETA 4h)
  - maria: add KV tenant-priority bump experiment (ETA tomorrow)
  - dina: design hedging formula and GPU-util guard (ETA EOD)

sam: ack. I'll also add alert: short-p50 > 2x baseline -> rollback.

maria: 👍 if experiment proves stable we can surface the knobs in Optimize for workload suggestions.

ash: cool — keeping thread for logs. ping me if you want access to canary traces. :mag:

ops-bot: Deploy succeeded on canary-3 and canary-4; canary-5 still updating.

perf-ci-bot: quick summary after 15m: short p50 improved 40%, KV hit-rate for shorts up to 0.62, long p95 +3% (within guard). continuing run.

ash: perfect. leave open, will post final when we have 24h run. thanks all :rocket:
